title: Launcher pair hardening (DEC-282 (a2) review findings on #744)
description: Follow-up to the opus security review of opum-ai/quest-cli#744 (approved at 75dabe81). Must land before the pair cut; lore-cli makes the same changes in #734 round 4 so the wrappers stay one design. N1: CHANGELOG names the wrong baseline (released 0.15.0 exited 1 when the child died by a signal; 128+n was unshipped round-1 code). N2: re-raise every terminating signal Node leaves at default; for SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ, SIGUSR1 exit 128+n instead (SIGUSR1 self-kill opens Node inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229). N3: wrap spawn() in try/catch so a synchronous throw (ENOEXEC, E2BIG) prints the same Quest could not start message, exit 1, no stack. N4: correct the setsid comment (no controlling terminal; SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU reason is wrong). N5: on-TTY test fails rather than skips when CI is set and script is missing; Number.isInteger on both pgids. N6: CHANGELOG residual names QCLI-571 and the TTY residual (on a TTY a SIGTERM reaches the child only, not its grandchildren). Not in scope: a tcgetpgrp-based pair-wide TTY test (design change routed to opum-doc).

acceptanceCriteria.text: CHANGELOG states the real baseline change and no longer lists a spawn-failure exit as a change
A child dying by SIGUSR1 or SIGPIPE makes the wrapper exit 128+n with no Debugger listening on stderr, proven by tests
A synchronous spawn throw (ENOEXEC) prints Quest could not start, exits 1 and prints no stack, proven by a test that goes red without the try/catch
The setsid comment is corrected and the CHANGELOG residual names QCLI-571 and the TTY grandchild residual
The on-TTY test fails when CI is set and script is missing, and both pgids are asserted integers
DEC-282 (a3) item 2: the child owns its process group only when none of fds 0, 1 and 2 is a terminal, proven by a stdin-piped/stdout-on-a-terminal test and an fd-0-only mutant that goes red on it
Review findings F1, F2, F3 and the CHANGELOG nit on #749 are taken
F4: a deterministic SIGUSR1 witness (a --require preload recording the self-kill) replaces stderr text as the only evidence, and the overclaiming comment is corrected

implementationNotes: PREDICTIONS written before the hardening mutants: (M10) spawn() try/catch removed: ONLY the ENOEXEC test goes red (stack trace on stderr). (M11) the NODE_HANDLED early return removed (self-kill for SIGPIPE/SIGXFSZ/SIGUSR1): the SIGUSR1 test goes red (inspector banner on stderr); the SIGPIPE test stays GREEN because Node ignores SIGPIPE, the self-kill does nothing and the 128+n fallback applies - that test pins behaviour, it is not a mutation witness. N5a/N5b/N4/N1/N6 are a CI-fail guard, assertions, a comment and docs: no mutant claimed.

Mutants vs predictions: M10 (try/catch removed) only the ENOEXEC test red - as predicted. M11 (NODE_HANDLED removed) only the SIGUSR1 test red; SIGPIPE stayed green - as predicted. Suite 13 pass. N5a: on-TTY test now fails (expect(hasScript)) when CI is set and script is missing. CI-runner question: the 75dabe81 source-gates job ran on ubuntu-24.04 (workflow runs-on) and its log lists test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts in the bun test command, but the log does not print per-test pass/skip lines, so whether the on-TTY test ran or skipped there is NOT confirmed from the log; with this change a missing script now fails CI instead of skipping. ACs checked on local evidence; CI is the remaining evidence.

CI RED at a9d44797: source-gates failed in the top_level group (exit 1); the prepublish log does not print the failing test, so the cause is INFERRED, not read. Hypothesis: the ENOEXEC test - libuv uses execvp, and glibc execvp retries an ENOEXEC file through /bin/sh, so on ubuntu a text file runs as a script (exit 127) instead of making spawn() throw, while macOS threw. Fix: the throw is now made deterministic with a --require preload that replaces child_process.spawn; the M10 mutant (try/catch removed) still goes red on it. Whether this clears CI is measured only by the next run.

DEC-282 (a3) item 2 built locally (NOT pushed: held until the leader relays the aae541f review verdict). ownGroup only when none of fds 0,1,2 is a terminal; new test runs `: | node wrapper` under script(1) so stdin is a pipe and stdout/stderr the pty, asserting equal pgids; the all-fds-terminal test and the all-piped own-group test are kept. PREDICTION written before the mutant: (M13) ownGroup checking fd 0 only: ONLY the stdin-piped/stdout-on-terminal test goes red; all other 13 stay green.
M13 (fd 0 only) result: ONLY the stdin-piped/stdout-on-terminal test red, 13 pass 1 fail - as predicted; restored 14 pass. Committed locally, not pushed.

#749 landed as approved at aae541fd (origin/dev 98c323a0). Next PR carries (a3) plus F1-F4 and the CHANGELOG nit. PREDICTION before re-measuring M11 (NODE_HANDLED early return removed): the SIGUSR1 test is red, the SIGPIPE test stays green (Node ignores SIGPIPE), all others green; the stronger inspector/9229 assertions are a witness-hardening, not a new mutant.

M11 re-measured with the strengthened witness: SIGUSR1 test red (stderr "Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/..."), SIGPIPE green, 13 pass 1 fail - as predicted; restored 14 pass. F1-F3 and the CHANGELOG nit are comment/doc changes (no mutant). (a3) three-fd group rule rides the same PR; QCLI-572 closes after that PR merges.

VERDICT: APPROVE — opum-ai/quest-cli#750 (QCLI-572) at e448171c, no blocking findings
SHA: e448171c

What I read and how: this is a read-only review and I ran nothing. I read bin/quest.cjs, test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts and CHANGELOG.md at the head. I also read the full PR diff, DEC-282 (opum-doc origin/dev text, all of it) and the #749 review at aae541f. The mutant results (M11 re-measured, M13) are the writer's, recorded on QCLI-572. I did not reproduce them. Runtime claims below come from reasoning about Node, libuv and POSIX behaviour, not from runs.

CHECKS
1. (a3) item 2: implemented as the ruling says.
   - bin/quest.cjs:67-68 is `ownGroup = platform !== "win32" && !isatty(0) && !isatty(1) && !isatty(2)`. The child joins its own group only when none of fds 0, 1 or 2 is a terminal, and stays in the caller's group when any one of them is. That matches the ruling's wording, including Node's tty.isatty.
   - The test the ruling requires is at test:303-319. It runs `: | node wrapper` under script(1), so stdin is a pipe and stdout and stderr are the pty, and it asserts equal pgids.
   - That test fails against the old `!isatty(0)` code: stdin is not a terminal, so the old code puts the child in its own group and the pgids differ. This matches the writer's M13 result: only this test went red.
2. (a2)/(a3) item 1 re-raise set: still matches.
   - NODE_HANDLED at :91 is exactly {SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ, SIGUSR1}.
   - The sequence at :150-158 is unchanged from what the #749 review approved: sweep, then set 128+n, then return early for those three, then remove the listeners and self-kill.
3. F1-F4 and the CHANGELOG nit: see the lines at the end.
4. Can the tests fail? Yes for the fd-0-only mutant. No for the single-clause mutants in finding 1.
5. Orphan prevention: no regression in the code paths.
   - The incident's shape, with all three fds piped, still makes the child its own group (detached), forwards signals to -pid and sweeps the group on exit.
   - The exit-handler sweep, the status passthrough and the sweep before the re-raise are all unchanged.
   - Informational, not a finding: a caller with stdin piped and stdout or stderr on a terminal now leaves the child in the caller's group, so a SIGTERM sent to the wrapper does not reach grandchildren. That is the trade-off (a3) ruled. The code comment (:54-61) and CHANGELOG.md:32-34 both state it.

FINDINGS
1. bin/quest.cjs:67-68 vs test:282-319 — NON-BLOCKING — Neither new clause has its own witness.
   - Remove only `&& !isatty(2)`: both pty tests stay green, because fd 1 is a terminal in the stdin-piped test.
   - Remove only `&& !isatty(1)`: also green, because fd 2 is a terminal there.
   - (a3) requires only the stdin-piped/stdout-on-a-terminal test, so this does not block.
   - Fix: add `: | node wrapper >/dev/null` (only stderr is a terminal; catches the dropped fd-2 clause) and `: | node wrapper 2>/dev/null` (only stdout is a terminal; catches the dropped fd-1 clause).
2. test:386-391 — NON-BLOCKING — The F4 witness is only partly fixed.
   - The new `/inspector/i` and `9229` assertions close the bound-port case: Node's "Starting inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229 failed" line contains both strings.
   - They do not close the timing race. Under M11 the self-kill does not kill the wrapper, so the exit code is still 128+n and the signal is still null. That leaves stderr text as the only witness. If the wrapper exits before the inspector writes anything, all three assertions pass.
   - The comment at :386-388 says "a slow inspector cannot keep a mutant green". That overclaims.
   - A deterministic witness would reuse the ENOEXEC test's --require preload: wrap process.kill and write a marker when it is called with (process.pid, "SIGUSR1").
3. bin/quest.cjs:126-128 — NON-BLOCKING — The F3 caveat states as fact that glibc's execvp retries an ENOEXEC file through /bin/sh. QCLI-572's own implementation note records that diagnosis as inferred, not read from a log, and a green CI on the preload-based test does not confirm it. Suggest "can retry" or "is believed to".
4. test:247-248 — NON-BLOCKING (nit) — A stale comment ("A missing `script` skips this test locally...") sits above `hasScript` and repeats the comment at :271-272, which is the one now attached to ptyTest. Delete the first copy.
5. .quest/tasks/QCLI-572.json — NON-BLOCKING — The task's title, description and five checked ACs still cover only the (a2) #744 findings. No AC covers the (a3) three-fd rule or F1-F4, so closing the task is not gated on the work this PR mainly carries. The implementation notes do record it.

PRIOR FINDINGS AND THE NIT
F1: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:54-61 names QCLI-571 and the grandchild residual when any fd is a terminal, and now says "Off a terminal a plain SIGTERM is fully handled".
F2: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:50-52 states the 128+n exception for SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1 (see NODE_HANDLED).
F3: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:126-128 carries the platform caveat. Finding 3 is about how firmly it is worded.
F4: PARTIAL — the inspector and 9229 assertions were added, which closes the bound-port case. The timing race remains and the comment overclaims (finding 2).
CHANGELOG nit: RESOLVED — CHANGELOG.md:35-37 now reads "Off a terminal, a plain SIGTERM ... is fully handled."

#761 landed (squash) at head 6794e36b11310dcdc1257d5c85ef084f1703dcfa after both source-gates rows, Tracker integrity and lore check were green on that exact head. VERDICT: APPROVE — opum-ai/quest-cli#761 (QCLI-572 AC8) at 6794e36b, no blocking findings
SHA: 6794e36b11310dcdc1257d5c85ef084f1703dcfa
Method: this was a read-only review and I ran nothing. I read the full diff (pr761.diff), and bin/quest.cjs, test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts and .quest/tasks/QCLI-572.json at HEAD. Every runtime claim below comes from reading the code and reasoning about Node and POSIX behaviour, not from a run.
ANSWERS TO THE FOUR QUESTIONS
(1) Comment-only: TRUE. The only bin/quest.cjs hunk changes `//` lines, :126-129 at HEAD. `startFailed(error); return;` appear only as unchanged context. The file mode stays 100755. The hunk goes from +9 to +10 lines, which is the one added comment line. No executable line changed.
(2) The SIGUSR1 witness is deterministic and not vacuous. The wrapper looks up `process.kill` as a property at each call (:75, :97, :159) and never captures it earlier, so the preload's replacement is the function the close handler reaches. Under the NODE_HANDLED mutant, :159 calls process.kill(process.pid, "SIGUSR1"). The preload writes the selfKill marker synchronously and swallows the call. Exit code 138 and signal null are unchanged, so the marker assertion at test:469 is the one that goes red, with no timing dependence. With correct code, :156 returns first and no marker is written. The armed marker (test:451/466) proves the preload loaded in the wrapper process, which is what makes the marker's absence meaningful. It does not by itself prove that interception works. Given the dynamic lookup, that is enough. The writer's mutant run is the evidence for the interception half. The preload goes only on the wrapper's argv (--require). There is no NODE_OPTIONS and no env, so it does not reach the /bin/sh child, and it never touches the test runner's own process.kill.
(3) The pty witnesses isolate their clauses and fail closed. `: | node … >/dev/null` leaves fds 0 and 1 off the terminal and fd 2 on it. Dropping `!isatty(2)` makes ownGroup true, the pgids differ, and only this test goes red. The fd-1 test mirrors it correctly with `2>/dev/null`. I walked both single-clause mutants through all five group tests. Each turns only its own test red, which matches the writer's prediction. A missing pty cannot pass vacuously. Without a pty all three fds are non-tty, the child gets its own group, and the equality assertion fails. If script cannot run at all, readPgids times out. Under CI, ptyTest asserts hasScript instead of skipping (test:280-287). A local machine without script skips silently, which is the accepted design.
(4) Flakiness and cleanup: no new risk found. The new tests reuse the existing pgidsUnderPty teardown (SIGKILL script, then await its exit) and rm the root in finally. The preload file and markers live inside root and are removed with it.
FINDINGS
1. test:328-368 vs bin/quest.cjs:67-68 — NON-BLOCKING (should-fix) — The fd-0 clause still has no witness of its own. If `!isatty(0)` alone is dropped, every group test stays green. Each pty test has fd 1 or fd 2 on the terminal, and the off-terminal test has none on it. The PR's own comment at :328-330 says "Each clause of the own-group predicate needs its own witness", and the file now meets that for two of three clauses. AC5's mutant was "fd 0 only", which drops clauses 1 and 2 together, so it does not cover this case. The real caller shape is an interactive `quest … >out.json 2>err.log` that needs a /dev/tty prompt or Ctrl-Z. Fix: add a ptyTest running `node <wrapper> >/dev/null 2>/dev/null`, so only stdin is a terminal, and predict that dropping `!isatty(0)` turns only that test red. Not blocking, because #750 finding 1 and (a3) asked only for fd 1 and fd 2.
2. test:488-490 — NON-BLOCKING (nit) — The same overclaim survives in a second place. bin/quest.cjs:126-129 is now hedged, but the ENOEXEC test comment still says, as fact, "glibc's execvp retries ENOEXEC through /bin/sh". This is #750 finding 3 in its other location. Suggested wording: "is believed to retry".
3. test:452-453 — NON-BLOCKING (optional hardening) — The preload matches only `signal === "SIGUSR1"`. A regression that self-kills with the numeric form (os.constants.signals.SIGUSR1, or 10) would bypass the marker and reach the real kill. Only the stderr assertions would remain, and they have the original timing race. Cheap fix: also match the numeric value. Optionally, record ANY self-kill and assert none happened for PIPE too. That would make the NODE_HANDLED SIGPIPE mutant detectable; it currently stays green, which the writer recorded as expected (M11 note).
4. test:471-475 — NIT — With the preload swallowing the SIGUSR1 self-kill, the inspector can no longer start, so the stderr assertions are close to dead in this test. They can fire only on a bypass path such as finding 3. The "Secondary only" comment is honest about this, so nothing needs to change.
AC8 SCORED ON BOTH CLAUSES: (a) A deterministic preload witness replaces stderr text as the only evidence: MET (test:441-470). (b) The overclaiming "a slow inspector cannot keep a mutant green" comment is corrected: MET. It is replaced by an accurate note at :431-440. AC8 is still unchecked at HEAD, which is expected before the merge.
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY WITHOUT A SHELL: the writer's mutant runs (fd-1 drop, fd-2 drop, SIGUSR1 removed from NODE_HANDLED) and the "16 pass" count, which I did not reproduce; whether CI's ubuntu runner actually runs the pty tests rather than skipping them (QCLI-572's earlier note says the CI log does not print per-test pass or skip lines, and I did not check the CI env for CI=true); whether any wrapper or child process survives the script SIGKILL teardown; macOS script(1) behaviour with stdin on /dev/null and a `: |` pipeline inside `sh -c`; whether Node's tty.isatty reports the util-linux script pty as a terminal on fds 1 and 2 under CI.

VERDICT: APPROVE at 460c06587e5e0914d49e7ddb8419a4f1aee7f2c5
Review of opum-ai/quest-cli#764 (QCLI-572 round 3): approve with no blocking findings and three NITs.

How I reviewed: read-only, and I ran nothing. I read the whole of pr764.diff, the #761 verdict, and these files at HEAD: bin/quest.cjs, test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts and .quest/tasks/QCLI-572.json. Every runtime claim below comes from reading the code, not from a run.

(a) #761 FINDINGS 1-4
| # | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 fd-0 clause has no witness of its own | CLOSED | test:370-391 (new ptyTest `node <wrapper> >/dev/null 2>/dev/null`) |
| 2 ENOEXEC test comment states the glibc execvp retry as fact | CLOSED | test:570-575, now "is believed to retry ... inferred, never read from a log". This matches the hedge at bin/quest.cjs:126-129 |
| 3 preload matches only the "SIGUSR1" string | CLOSED, including the optional half | preload test:451-472 matches `"SIGUSR1"` or `os.constants.signals.SIGUSR1`. It records every self-kill as `swallowed:` or `forwarded:`. The marker-absent assertion at test:505-507 now runs for PIPE as well as USR1 |
| 4 stderr assertions are close to dead | LEFT DELIBERATELY | test:508-512. The "Secondary only" comment stays and is still accurate |

On finding 3's optional half: if SIGPIPE is removed from NODE_HANDLED, :159 calls process.kill(pid, "SIGPIPE"). The preload writes `forwarded:SIGPIPE` and forwards the call, Node ignores the signal, and the test goes red on test:507. #761 recorded that the M11 SIGPIPE case stayed green; it is now detectable.

(b) DOES THE NEW TEST DISTINGUISH THE fd-0 CLAUSE? Yes. Two different mutants are involved, and your scope text mixes them, so here they are separately. I walked each one across all six group tests (the off-terminal test at :239 plus the five pty tests at :289, :310, :332, :352 and :375).
- Drop-fd-0 mutant: `ownGroup = platform !== "win32" && !isatty(1) && !isatty(2)` (bin/quest.cjs:67-68). This is #761 finding 1.
  - New test (:375): stdin is the pty and fds 1 and 2 are /dev/null. ownGroup becomes true, so detached setsid gives the child its own group. Then child != wrapperGroup and `expect(child).toBe(wrapperGroup)` at :386 goes RED.
  - Every other test stays green. :239 has no tty anywhere, so it is already own-group. :289 has fd 1 on the pty. :310 and :352 have fd 1 on the pty. :332 has fd 2 on the pty.
  - Prediction: only :375 goes red.
- AC5's "fd 0 only" mutant: `ownGroup = ... && !isatty(0)`.
  - The new test stays GREEN, because isatty(0) is true, so ownGroup is false.
  - :310, :332 and :352 catch it, since stdin is piped in all three.
  - So the new test is not the witness for AC5's mutant. It does not need to be.
- With this PR, each of the three clauses has a test that goes red when only that clause is dropped.
- Vacuity under CI, for the new test specifically: it fails closed.
  - With CI set and `script` missing, ptyTest runs and `expect(hasScript).toBe(true)` (:284) fails. It does not skip.
  - If script runs but no tty is allocated, all three fds are non-tty, ownGroup is true, the pgids differ, and the equality assertion fails.
  - If script cannot run at all, readPgids times out.
  - If ps yields nothing, the Number.isInteger checks or the split-length wait catch it.
  - An equality assertion is the right shape here. A `not.toBe` would pass vacuously.
- Evidence gap: QCLI-572 at HEAD records no prediction and no run for the drop-fd-0 mutant in this round. The last notes are M13 and M11. So the "goes red" claim in the comment at :373 rests on my reading and yours, not on a measurement. See F4.

(c) NUMERIC SIGUSR1 MATCH: covered, and the string form is intact.
- `signal === "SIGUSR1" || signal === USR1` (preload :462), with `USR1 = os.constants.signals.SIGUSR1` (:458).
- It matches the platform's own value: 10 on Linux, 30 on darwin. A hardcoded 10 would have been wrong on darwin, where 10 is SIGBUS.
- The "raw number" is therefore covered exactly when it equals the platform constant, which is the correct scope.
- The string arm comes first and is unchanged.
- Other spellings ("USR1", "10") are not a real path, because process.kill throws ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL on them.
- The new instrument test (:524-563) runs a driver that calls `process.kill(process.pid, <numeric>)` and requires the marker to read exactly `swallowed:<n>`. If the `|| signal === USR1` arm is removed, the marker reads `forwarded:<n>` and the test goes red. That makes it a real control of the numeric arm, and it is deterministic.

(d) TEST-ONLY: confirmed against the diff file. pr764.diff has exactly one `diff --git` header, test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts. Its last hunk (@@ -487,8 +569,10 @@) closes at 8 old and 10 new lines, so the file is not truncated. No file under bin/ or src/ appears in it. Also, bin/quest.cjs:126-129 at HEAD carries the hedge #761 described. What I could not do without git is compare bin/ against dev directly, so "nothing under bin/ differs from dev" is your claim, consistent with what I read but not measured by me.

(e) NEW RISKS
- The new pty test reuses pgidsUnderPty and its teardown unchanged, with the same macOS (`-q /dev/null sh -c`) and Linux (`-qec "sh -c '...'" /dev/null`) script syntax.
- It adds no new timing dependence.
- Its command has no single quotes, so the Linux quoting holds.
- Stdin on the pty is the same exposure the existing all-fds test (:289) already has. Neither the wrapper nor the PGIDS stand-in reads stdin, so script's handling of stdin EOF does not matter.
- The preload's `forwarded:` arm fires only for pid === process.pid. sweepGroup uses -child.pid and signalChild uses child.kill, so neither can write the marker on a correct run.
- I found no flakiness.

NEW FINDINGS
F1 — NIT — test:373. "this goes red iff `!isatty(0)` is dropped" overclaims. Other mutants also turn it red, for example dropping every clause or forcing `detached: true`. Fix: "goes red if `!isatty(0)` alone is dropped", which matches the "if" wording at :331 and :351.
F2 — NIT — test:520. "QCLI-572 round 3 finding 3" does not resolve: the finding comes from the #761 review (round 2), and this PR is round 3. Fix: "#761 review finding 3".
F3 — NIT — test:552-555. The comment says the swallow means "the driver survived", and `expect(result.signal).toBeNull()` does not discriminate, because Node survives a real SIGUSR1 either way (it starts the inspector). The marker read at :556 is the only discriminator. Fix: say so in the comment, or replace the signal check with `expect(result.code).toBe(0)` plus a note that the marker is the witness.
F4 — SHOULD (record, not code) — .quest/tasks/QCLI-572.json. Two parts:
  - No implementation note records a prediction, or a result, for the drop-fd-0 mutant (`!isatty(1) && !isatty(2)`, predicted to turn only :375 red) or for the preload with the numeric arm removed (predicted to turn only :524 red). M10, M11 and M13 all have one.
  - No AC covers this round. AC5's text ("fd-0-only mutant") names the other mutant, so citing AC5 for this work would conflate the two.
  - Fix: run both mutants and record prediction then result before the bump bytes. Decide whether an AC9 is wanted or a note suffices.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
- Neither mutant run.
- The suite pass count.
- That CI's ubuntu runner actually executes the pty tests. The earlier QCLI-572 note says the log does not print per-test pass or skip lines.
- That util-linux script presents the pty on fd 0 inside `sh -c` when its own stdin is /dev/null. The :289 test depends on the same thing.
